Regarding our agentic data sourcing, I realized one edge case. Some datasets publish their data in more than one part. In that case, our agent sometimes only recommends Part 1 as source but Part 2 is nowhere.

Why isn't our agent smart enough to search for other parts in that case?

I’m using the debugging skill to trace this from shortlist generation through approval, without changing anything. I’ll inspect the sourcing contracts and tests to identify whether “other parts” are discoverable, filtered, or simply never queried.

content.text: The first concrete clue is that the system does not run an open-ended “find the family” investigation after discovering a source. Its model only extracts search vocabulary; three fixed query templates do discovery, and extra searches happen only when mandatory evidence is missing. I’m checking the native-link behavior now, because that determines whether Part 2 can appear without search returning it directly.

It’s not a model-intelligence problem; it’s an orchestration gap.

The current scout:

- Uses the LLM only to extract search vocabulary, then runs three fixed queries ([planning.py](/Users/I776111/.codex/worktrees/b9e2/ysamet/data_sourcing/src/data_sourcing/planning.py:147)).
- Does not react to a title like “Part I” by launching a “find remaining parts” search.
- Runs follow-up searches only when mandatory requirements lack evidence. If Part I satisfies the contract, discovery stops ([graph.py](/Users/I776111/.codex/worktrees/b9e2/ysamet/data_sourcing/src/data_sourcing/graph.py:471)).
- Discovers siblings only through explicit supported URLs in native text ([graph.py](/Users/I776111/.codex/worktrees/b9e2/ysamet/data_sourcing/src/data_sourcing/graph.py:418)). The Zenodo adapter does not inspect dataset-series metadata or infer Part II from Part I’s title ([native.py](/Users/I776111/.codex/worktrees/b9e2/ysamet/data_sourcing/src/data_sourcing/adapters/native.py:601)).
- Can also lose linked sources at the eight-candidate cutoff because direct search results are placed before URLs extracted from their snippets ([canonicalize.py](/Users/I776111/.codex/worktrees/b9e2/ysamet/data_sourcing/src/data_sourcing/adapters/canonicalize.py:87)).
- Recommends one top candidate. The recent multi-source feature only lets users approve additional candidates already present in the shortlist; it does not discover missing parts.

Our bundled KUKA fixture explicitly lists both Part I and Part II, so existing tests exercise the happy path and mask the general weakness.

The correct improvement is a deterministic “dataset-family completeness” stage: detect multipart indicators, query native relationship metadata and exact-title siblings, verify each part separately, and group them without merging their source identities. Until that exists, the agent is effectively finding eligible records—not proving it found the complete publication family.

I’ll implement this as a bounded dataset-family completion stage, preserving each part as a separate candidate and source identity. I’m using the git workflow, incremental implementation, and source-driven development skills because this spans discovery logic, provider metadata, contracts, and regression tests.
